editorial:
Imagine meeting a famous artist who can see right through your secrets. That is exactly what happens when editor Kyoka Izumi chats with the eccentric Rohan Kishibe. Kyoka is bragging about her new star manga artist, Mika Saion, who is selling millions of copies. But Rohan has a weird feeling that something is wrong. He points out a huge red flag: Kyoka has never actually met Mika in person and only talks to her brother on the phone. This sets up a creepy, puzzling vibe as you follow Kyoka to the Saion estate to find out why the star artist refuses to speak or show her face.

The mystery unfolds at a great pace, and the acting makes the tension feel real. You will love how the story tricks you before revealing the truth. The only downside is that some parts feel a bit slow, but the big reveal makes it worth it. If you want the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the artistic details. Or, if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move. It is a perfect pick for anyone who likes a good puzzle.
endingExplained: You find out that Mika Saion does not actually exist as a separate person. Her brother Soshi has been using a strange power to create the manga and pretend to be his sister. He manipulated Kyoka and everyone else to keep the fame for himself. Once Rohan uses his abilities to expose the truth, the fake image of Mika vanishes. Soshi is finally caught, and the mystery of the silent artist is solved for good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological mysteries and quirky characters.
